coronaryAngiogram.title: Coronary Angiogram: Purpose, Procedure & What to Expect
coronaryAngiogram.subheading: Comprehensive Guide by InDocsCare Medical Services

whatIs.title: What is a Coronary Angiogram?
whatIs.content1: A <bold>coronary angiogram</bold> is an advanced heart imaging procedure that uses X-ray technology and a special contrast dye to create detailed visuals of the coronary arteries—the blood vessels that supply oxygen-rich blood to your heart.
whatIs.content2: It is one of the most accurate diagnostic tools for identifying <bold>blockages, narrowing, or abnormalities</bold> in these arteries. Doctors frequently use this procedure to investigate chest pain, shortness of breath, or other symptoms of heart disease, and to plan the most effective treatment options.

why.title: Why is a Coronary Angiogram Performed?
why.diagnosing: <bold>Diagnosing Coronary Artery Disease (CAD):</bold> Detects narrowing or blockages that could cause heart attacks.
why.assessing: <bold>Assessing Heart Function:</bold> Evaluates how well blood is flowing to your heart muscle.
why.guiding: <bold>Guiding Treatment:</bold> Helps doctors decide whether you need medications, stents, angioplasty, or heart bypass surgery.
why.preventing: <bold>Preventing Future Events:</bold> Identifies risks before they turn into major heart problems.

preparation.title: How to Prepare for Your Coronary Angiogram
preparation.content: Proper preparation ensures safe and accurate results:
preparation.medicalHistory: <bold>Medical History: </bold>Inform your doctor about any medications, supplements, or allergies (especially to iodine or contrast dye).
preparation.medicationAdjustment: <bold>Medication Adjustment:</bold> You may need to pause certain medications such as blood thinners.
preparation.fasting: <bold>Fasting: </bold>Avoid eating or drinking for 6 to 8 hours before the test.
preparation.arrangements: <bold>Arrangements:</bold> Bring a companion to drive you home, as sedatives may make you feel drowsy.

procedure.title: What Happens During the Procedure?
procedure.pretext: The test takes place in a specialized catheterization lab (cath lab) and generally lasts 30–60 minutes.
procedure.setup: <bold>Setup:</bold> You will lie on a table, and an IV line will be inserted for medications and contrast dye. The insertion site (groin or wrist) will be cleaned and numbed with local anesthesia.
procedure.catheterInsertion: <bold>Catheter Insertion:</bold> A thin, flexible catheter is guided through a blood vessel to your heart using X-ray images.
procedure.dyeInjection: <bold>Dye Injection:</bold> The contrast dye highlights your coronary arteries, making blockages or abnormalities visible on X-ray images.
procedure.imaging: <bold>Imaging:</bold> Several images will be taken to thoroughly examine your heart’s blood vessels.
procedure.completion: <bold>Completion and Recovery:</bold> After the catheter is removed, pressure will be applied to the site to prevent bleeding. You may be fitted with a bandage or compression device.

interpreting.title: Interpreting Your Results
interpreting.normal: <bold>Normal Results:</bold> No significant narrowing or blockages—healthy coronary arteries.
interpreting.partialBlockages: <bold>Partial Blockages:</bold> May require lifestyle changes, medications, or stenting.
interpreting.severeBlockages: <bold>Severe Blockages:</bold> May necessitate angioplasty, stenting, or bypass surgery (CABG).
interpreting.otherAbnormalities: <bold>Other Abnormalities:</bold> Such as aneurysms or arterial spasms, may require specific interventions.
interpreting.note: Your cardiologist will discuss your results in detail and recommend the best course of action. You also can send us your reports to get proper detail of treatment.

commonUses.title: Common Uses of a Coronary Angiogram
commonUses.investigateSymptoms: Investigating unexplained<bold> chest pain</bold> or<bold> shortness of breath</bold>
commonUses.evaluateDamage: Evaluating damage after a heart attack
commonUses.surgeryPlanning: Planning for heart surgeries or procedures
commonUses.angioplastyPlanning: Planning for<bold> Angioplasty with Stent Placement (Coronary Angioplasty)</bold>
commonUses.monitoringHighRisk: Monitoring heart health in high-risk patients

accuracyFactors.title: Factors Affecting Test Accuracy
accuracyFactors.contrastDyeAllergy: Allergic reactions to the contrast dye
accuracyFactors.calciumDeposits: Dense calcium deposits in the arteries

mild.title: Mild Blockages
mild.lifestyleChanges: Lifestyle changes (heart-healthy diet, regular exercise, quitting smoking)
mild.medications: Medications (cholesterol control, blood pressure management, antiplatelet drugs)

severe.title: Severe Blockages
severe.cabg: <bold>Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (CABG)</bold> — to restore blood flow around blockages
severe.advancedTechNote1: InDocsCare provide you upgraded latest modern technologies in cardiac procedures & Surgeries
severe.advancedTechNote2: Now CABG can be performed using minimally invasive techniques through a small incision on the side of the chest — no need for opening the entire chest.
severe.advancedTechNote3: Our expert and highly experienced doctors utilize the latest advanced technologies to perform stent procedures with excellent success rates. In many cases, even severe blockages of 95% or more can be effectively treated with modern stenting techniques. However, outcomes may vary depending on each patient’s individual condition.
severe.note: <bold>Note:</bold> You can send us your medical reports to get our experts' opinion.

benefits.title: Benefits of a Coronary Angiogram
benefits.accurateDiagnosis: <bold>Accurate Diagnosis</bold> — Clear images of coronary arteries
benefits.minimallyInvasive: <bold>Minimally Invasive </bold>— Small incision with fast recovery
benefits.angioplastyStenting: <bold>Angioplasty & Stenting</bold> — No cut, No open procedures
benefits.immediateResults: <bold>Immediate Results </bold>— Get quick answers during the procedure

final.title: Final Thoughts
final.content1: A coronary angiogram is a vital procedure for the early detection and management of <bold>coronary artery disease</bold>. By providing highly detailed insights into your heart’s blood flow, it enables doctors to act promptly—helping prevent future complications and improving heart health outcomes.
final.content2: If you or a loved one is experiencing heart-related symptoms or has risk factors for CAD, consult your healthcare provider or reach out to <bold>InDocsCare Medical Services </bold>to learn whether a coronary angiogram may be right for you.

angioplasty.title: Coronary Angioplasty (PTCA/PCI) — Advanced Treatment for Blocked Heart Arteries
angioplasty.subtitle: Comprehensive Guide by InDocsCare Medical Services

whatIs.description1: <bold>Percutaneous Transluminal Coronary Angioplasty (PTCA)</bold>, also known as <bold>Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI)</bold>, is a minimally invasive procedure used to open blocked heart arteries.he goal is to restore healthy blood flow to the heart muscle (myocardium), preventing heart attacks and relieving chest pain caused by<bold> coronary artery disease (CAD)</bold>.
whatIs.description2: CAD is caused by plaque buildup (atherosclerosis) inside the arteries, leading to narrowed or blocked vessels.

indications.title: When is PTCA Recommended?
indications.nonResponsiveAngina: <bold>Patients with angina not responding to medication</bold>
indications.note: <bold>Note: take doctor’s opinion before proceeding or contact InDocsCare for experts suggestions</bold>

procedure.title: How is PTCA Performed?
procedure.catheterInsertion: A<bold> catheter </bold>is inserted through the femoral or radial artery.
procedure.balloonGuidance: Using advanced imaging, a<bold> balloon</bold> is guided to the blocked artery.
procedure.balloonInflation: The balloon inflates to open the artery, and a <bold>stent </bold>(a small metal mesh tube) is placed to keep it open.
procedure.duration: The procedure typically takes<bold> 30 minutes to 2 hours</bold>.
procedure.expertDoctors: Performed by expert<bold> interventional cardiologists </bold>at top hospitals.
procedure.advancedCare: We have most experienced Doctors & Advanced technology

safety.title: Safety & Complications
safety.safeProcedure: PTCA is a highly safe procedure with excellent success rates.However, risks may include:
safety.minorBleeding: Minor bleeding or bruising at the insertion site
safety.kidneyStrain: Temporary kidney strain from contrast dye

postProcedure.title: Post-Procedure Care
postProcedure.resumeActivity: Resume light activities within a few days
postProcedure.lifestyleAdjustments: Lifestyle adjustments: <bold>healthy diet, exercise, stress reduction</bold>

whyInDocsCare.title: Why InDocsCare?
whyInDocsCare.experiencedDoctors: <bold>Our experienced cardiac specialists</bold> perform angioplasty even for complex cases with<bold> high success rates,</bold> including blockages above 90%. We collaborate with leading hospitals and offer <bold>personalized patient care</bold> — from consultation to complete recovery.

angioplastyStenting.title: Coronary Angioplasty & Stenting
angioplastyStenting.subtitle: Comprehensive Guide by InDocsCare Medical Services

overview.description1: Coronary angioplasty is a minimally invasive procedure to open blocked heart arteries (coronary arteries) and restore healthy blood flow to the heart muscle.Using a thin catheter with a small balloon at the tip, doctors inflate the balloon inside the artery to widen it.Often, a tiny mesh tube called a <bold>stent </bold>is placed to keep the artery open and reduce the risk of future narrowing.
overview.description2: Also known as <bold>Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI)</bold>, this treatment can be scheduled to manage heart disease or performed urgently during a heart attack.

whyNeed.description: Coronary angioplasty treats <bold>coronary artery disease (CAD)</bold> — a condition where arteries are narrowed by cholesterol plaques (atherosclerosis), limiting blood flow to the heart. You may be a candidate if:
whyNeed.title: Why You May Need Angioplasty
whyNeed.reason1: Medications or lifestyle changes haven’t improved symptoms
whyNeed.reason3: Emergency treatment is needed for a heart attack
whyNeed.note: In some cases, <bold>coronary artery bypass surgery (CABG)</bold> may be a better option.

preparation.title: Preparing for Your Procedure
preparation.description: For scheduled angioplasty, your heart doctor (cardiologist) will review your health and guide your preparation. Typical steps include:
preparation.step2: Adjusting or stopping blood thinners if needed
preparation.step3: Fasting for several hours before the procedure
preparation.emergencyNote: In emergencies (like heart attacks), there may be no preparation time.

expectation.title: What to Expect
expectation.before: <bold>Before:</bold> You’ll be monitored closely — heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen, etc.
expectation.during: <bold>During:</bold> Performed in a hospital, you’ll remain awake or lightly sedated. The cardiologist inserts a catheter through a blood vessel in the arm or leg, using X-ray guidance and contrast dye to identify blockages. A balloon inflates to open the artery, and a stent is placed to maintain blood flow. The procedure typically lasts 1-2 hours.
expectation.after: <bold>After:</bold> You may stay in the hospital overnight. Recovery instructions usually include resting, avoiding heavy lifting for 24 hours, and taking prescribed blood thinners to prevent clots.

recovery.title: Recovery & Results
recovery.benefit: Angioplasty with stenting <bold>improves blood flow </bold>and reduces chest pain. It can also prevent heart attacks.However, it doesn’t cure artery disease — healthy lifestyle changes are key to long-term heart health.

beatingHeartCABG.title: Beating Heart Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (BHCABG)
beatingHeartCABG.aka: Also Known as Off-Pump CABG Surgery
beatingHeartCABG.description: <bold>Beating Heart CABG (BHCABG)</bold>, or<bold> Off-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass (OPCAB)</bold>, is an advanced cardiac surgery technique used to treat <bold>blocked coronary arteries </bold>— without stopping the heart or using a heart-lung machine.
beatingHeartCABG.howItWorksTitle: How Does Beating Heart CABG Work?
beatingHeartCABG.howItWorksDescription: During this <bold>minimally invasive heart bypass surgery</bold>, the heart continues to beat while the surgeon performs the bypass graft. A specialized<bold> stabilization device </bold>gently holds the precise area of the heart where the graft is attached — using flexible suction pods. These pods <bold>lift the heart tissue</bold> (without pressing down), allowing the surgeon to safely perform the bypass while preserving natural heart function.
beatingHeartCABG.benefitLowerRisk: Lower risk of stroke and complications
beatingHeartCABG.benefitFasterRecovery: Faster recovery compared to traditional CABG
beatingHeartCABG.benefitBetterForHighRisk: Better option for high-risk or elderly patients
beatingHeartCABG.servicesDescription: <bold>InDocsCare Medical Services</bold> connects you with leading heart surgeons and hospitals in India specializing in<bold> Beating Heart CABG </bold>— offering advanced, safer, and more efficient treatment for coronary artery disease.

heartValveReplacement.title: Heart Valve Replacement Surgery
heartValveReplacement.introDescription: <bold>Heart valve replacement </bold>is a life-saving procedure that restores normal blood flow through the heart by replacing a damaged or diseased valve with a<bold> biological </bold>or <bold>mechanical</bold> valve.
heartValveReplacement.symptomDescription: When heart valves become narrowed (stenosis), stiff, or leaky (regurgitation), they can no longer regulate blood flow efficiently — leading to fatigue, shortness of breath, chest pain, and serious heart complications. In such cases, <bold>heart valve replacement</bold> is often the best treatment option.
heartValveReplacement.biologicalValvesPoint1: Made from cow, pig, or human donor tissue
heartValveReplacement.biologicalValvesPoint2: Don’t typically require lifelong blood thinners
heartValveReplacement.mechanicalValvesPoint1: Made from durable metals or carbon
heartValveReplacement.mechanicalValvesPoint3: Requires lifelong blood-thinning medications (to prevent blood clots)
heartValveReplacement.optionTAVR: <bold>Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR)</bold> — a catheter-based procedure, ideal for high-risk or older patients
heartValveReplacement.optionRoss: <bold>Ross Procedure </bold>— best for young patients with aortic valve disease
heartValveReplacement.minimallyInvasiveTitle: Minimally Invasive Heart Valve Surgery (No Chest Cut)
heartValveReplacement.minimallyInvasiveDescription: <bold>Minimally Invasive Valve Surgery </bold>allows surgeons to repair or replace heart valves without the need for a large chest incision (sternotomy). Instead of cutting through the breastbone, the surgeon accesses the heart through small keyhole incisions between the ribs — often just 2 to 4 cm wide. In many cases, the procedure can even be performed via <bold>Transcatheter techniques</bold> (such as TAVR) through a blood vessel in the leg — with <bold>no chest incision at all</bold>.
heartValveReplacement.minimallyInvasiveNote: Note: For more detail and Doctor’s opinion contact us
heartValveReplacement.recoveryDescription: Most patients recover in<bold> 1–2 months</bold>, depending on the type of surgery. Minimally invasive options allow faster recovery with fewer risks.
heartValveReplacement.recoverySuccessRate: <bold>Success rates</bold> are very high: modern procedures like <bold>TAVR</bold> offer a success rate of <bold>over 95%.</bold>
heartValveReplacement.recoveryNote: Note: Results may vary from patient to patient. Send us your medical reports we will confirm it with our senior doctors.
heartValveReplacement.servicesDescription: <bold>InDocsCare Medical Services </bold>connects patients with India's top cardiac surgeons and world-class hospitals, providing affordable and expert care for <bold>heart valve replacement surgery</bold>.

minimallyInvasiveMitralRepair.title: Minimally Invasive Mitral Valve Repair: Advanced Treatment Without Open-Heart Surgery
minimallyInvasiveMitralRepair.description: <bold>Minimally Invasive Mitral Valve Repair </bold>is a modern procedure that treats diseased mitral valves without cutting the chest bone or requiring traditional open-heart surgery. Using tiny incisions and advanced surgical tools (often with robotic assistance), this approach restores proper blood flow between the left atrium and left ventricle—offering faster recovery, fewer risks, and less scarring.
minimallyInvasiveMitralRepair.whenRecommendedTitle: When is Minimally Invasive Mitral Valve Surgery Recommended?
minimallyInvasiveMitralRepair.whenRecommendedPoint1: <bold>Mitral Valve Regurgitation </bold>(leaky valve due to floppy valve flaps)
minimallyInvasiveMitralRepair.whenRecommendedPoint2: <bold>Mitral Valve Stenosis </bold>(narrowed valve reducing blood flow)
minimallyInvasiveMitralRepair.whenRecommendedPoint4: Failure of previous mitral valve procedures
minimallyInvasiveMitralRepair.procedureStep1: Pre-surgery tests: Echocardiogram, CT scan (if needed)
minimallyInvasiveMitralRepair.procedureStep3: A small 2-3 inch incision is made near the breastbone
minimallyInvasiveMitralRepair.procedureStep4: Tiny cameras and instruments are inserted to repair or replace the mitral valve
minimallyInvasiveMitralRepair.procedureStep5: Procedures may include <bold>valve repair (ring annuloplasty) or valve replacement</bold>
minimallyInvasiveMitralRepair.procedureStep7: Minimal scarring with stitches after the procedure
minimallyInvasiveMitralRepair.recoveryPoint2: Hospital discharge in<bold> 3-4 days</bold> (depending on condition)
minimallyInvasiveMitralRepair.recoveryPoint3: Follow balanced diet, breathing exercises, and stop smoking
minimallyInvasiveMitralRepair.recoveryPoint5: Most patients resume normal activity faster than with open-heart surgery
minimallyInvasiveMitralRepair.benefitLowerInfectionRisk: Lower risk of infection and complications
minimallyInvasiveMitralRepair.benefitAffordable: More affordable with fewer hospital bills
minimallyInvasiveMitralRepair.whyChoosePoint1: Team of expert cardiac surgeons with years of experience
minimallyInvasiveMitralRepair.whyChoosePoint2: Advanced minimally invasive and robotic heart surgery techniques
minimallyInvasiveMitralRepair.whyChoosePoint3: High success rates and patient satisfaction
minimallyInvasiveMitralRepair.whyChoosePoint4: Focused on faster recovery, minimal pain, and reduced complications
minimallyInvasiveMitralRepair.whyChoosePoint5: Comprehensive pre-surgery consultation & personalized post-surgery care
minimallyInvasiveMitralRepair.closingCallToAction: Choose <bold>Minimally Invasive Mitral Valve Repair</bold> with <bold>InDocsCare </bold>— safe, effective, and patient-friendly.

coronaryArteryBypass.title: Coronary Artery Bypass Surgery (CABG): Restoring Heart Health
coronaryArteryBypass.introDescription: <bold>Coronary Artery Bypass Surgery </bold>(CABG), also known <bold>as heart bypass surgery</bold>, creates a new route for blood flow around blocked or narrowed arteries in the heart. Using a healthy blood vessel from your chest or leg, surgeons bypass the blocked artery, improving circulation to the heart muscle and reducing symptoms like chest pain and shortness of breath.
coronaryArteryBypass.introDescription2: While CABG can significantly enhance quality of life and lower the risk of heart-related complications.
coronaryArteryBypass.whenRecommendedPoint1: Severe blockage in the left main heart artery
coronaryArteryBypass.whenRecommendedPoint4: Reduced heart function (weakened lower heart chamber)
coronaryArteryBypass.whenRecommendedPoint5: When stenting or angioplasty is not possible or has failed
coronaryArteryBypass.whenRecommendedPoint6: Emergency treatment after a heart attack
coronaryArteryBypass.procedureStep2: Surgeons access the heart through an incision in the chest
coronaryArteryBypass.procedureStep3: A healthy blood vessel (graft) is attached to bypass the blocked artery
coronaryArteryBypass.procedureStep4: Surgery typically lasts <bold>3 to 6 hours</bold>, depending on the number of blockages
coronaryArteryBypass.procedureStep5: Variations include <bold>off-pump (beating-heart) surgery </bold>or <bold>minimally invasive techniques</bold> (small incisions)
coronaryArteryBypass.recoveryPoint1: ICU stay: 1–2 days; total hospital stay: typically 5–7 days
coronaryArteryBypass.recoveryPoint3: Significant symptom relief and improved heart function
coronaryArteryBypass.recoveryPoint4: Lifelong benefits when combined with lifestyle changes (healthy diet, exercise, quitting smoking)
coronaryArteryBypass.recoveryPoint5: Cardiac rehabilitation is recommended for optimal recovery
coronaryArteryBypass.riskNote: Your overall risk depends on factors such as age, diabetes, kidney disease, or lung disease.
coronaryArteryBypass.lifeAfterDescription: With proper follow-up care, most patients enjoy improved energy levels and better quality of life for years after surgery. Continued heart-healthy living is key to long-term success:
coronaryArteryBypass.lifeAfterPoint6: Control blood pressure, cholesterol, and diabetes
coronaryArteryBypass.servicesDescription: <bold>Choose InDocsCare Medical Services for expert cardiac care, trusted surgeons, and world-class post-operative support</bold>. Experience faster recovery and personalized treatment plans designed for your heart health.

MinimallyInvasiveCABG.title: Minimally Invasive Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (CABG)
MinimallyInvasiveCABG.whatIsDescription: Minimally Invasive Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (CABG) is an advanced heart surgery used to treat blocked or narrowed coronary arteries. Unlike traditional open-heart surgery, this procedure is performed through a small incision between the ribs — without cutting the breastbone and often without stopping the heart or using a heart-lung machine.
MinimallyInvasiveCABG.whatIsDescription2: During the surgery, a healthy blood vessel is taken from the chest or another part of the body and grafted onto the blocked artery to restore blood flow to the heart muscle.
MinimallyInvasiveCABG.benefit2: Lower risk of infection and stroke
MinimallyInvasiveCABG.benefit4: Faster recovery — return to normal activities in 10-15 days
MinimallyInvasiveCABG.benefit6: Reduced blood loss and fewer transfusions
MinimallyInvasiveCABG.whoShouldConsiderDescription: Ideal for patients with coronary artery disease who:
MinimallyInvasiveCABG.consider2: Have other health conditions (diabetes, COPD, obesity)
MinimallyInvasiveCABG.consider3: May not tolerate traditional open-heart surgery
MinimallyInvasiveCABG.consider4: Final decision, doctor will take according health condition of patient.
MinimallyInvasiveCABG.notSuitableDescription: Patients with prior chest surgery, radiation therapy, or significant scar tissue. Suitability is assessed on a case-by-case basis by our expert heart surgeons.
MinimallyInvasiveCABG.procedureDescription: Performed under general anesthesia, the surgeon makes a small 2-2.5 inch incision between the ribs.Using special instruments and a camera (endoscope), they graft the healthy blood vessel to bypass the blocked artery.If multiple arteries are blocked, multiple grafts can be done during the same procedure.
MinimallyInvasiveCABG.recovery3: Most patients can resume daily activities within 10-15 days
MinimallyInvasiveCABG.recovery4: Much faster recovery compared to 3-4 months after traditional CABG
MinimallyInvasiveCABG.risksDescription: While risks are lower than traditional surgery, complications such as bleeding, infection, breathing issues, or graft failure may still occur, although rarely.
MinimallyInvasiveCABG.resultsDescription: Patients typically enjoy long-lasting relief from chest pain and improved heart function. Healthy lifestyle changes and medication help maintain these benefits.
MinimallyInvasiveCABG.ctaDescription: <bold>Contact InDocsCare Medical Services</bold> today to learn if Minimally Invasive CABG is right for you.

doubleValveSurgery.title: Double Valve Surgery: Procedure, Benefits & Recovery
doubleValveSurgery.description: <bold>Double valve surgery</bold> is a life-saving procedure where two heart valves—commonly the aortic and mitral, or mitral and tricuspid—are repaired or replaced in a single operation. This surgery is crucial when valves are narrowed (stenosis) or leaky (regurgitation), leading to fatigue, chest pain, dizziness, shortness of breath, and swelling in the legs.
doubleValveSurgery.whyNeededDescription: Diseased heart valves disrupt blood flow, forcing the heart to work harder. If untreated, this may result in serious complications. When both valves are severely damaged, <bold>double valve replacement or repair </bold>restores healthy circulation and improves quality of life.
doubleValveSurgery.valveTypeMechanical: <bold>Mechanical Valves: </bold>Durable (10–20 years), made from advanced materials; lifelong blood thinners required.
doubleValveSurgery.valveTypeBiologic: <bold>Biologic Valves:</bold> Made from human or animal tissue; may not require long-term blood thinners but have a shorter lifespan.
doubleValveSurgery.diagnosisDescription: To evaluate heart valve function and plan surgery, doctors use:
doubleValveSurgery.recoveryDescription: Post-surgery, patients stay in the ICU for close monitoring. Breathing support is provided initially, followed by gradual reintroduction of normal activities. Most patients are discharged in a few days and continue recovery at home with medical guidance.
doubleValveSurgery.aftercarePoint1: Watch for swelling, fever, or redness near the incision.
doubleValveSurgery.aftercarePoint2: Keep the area clean and follow your care team’s advice.
doubleValveSurgery.aftercarePoint3: Gradually return to light activities and regular check-ups

singleBypassValveReplacement.title: Single Bypass and Valve Replacement Surgery
singleBypassValveReplacement.subtitle: Learn about Single Bypass and Valve Replacement Surgery: how it improves heart function, what to expect, and recovery tips. Trusted care at InDocsCare Medical Services.
singleBypassValveReplacement.description: <bold>Single Bypass and Valve Replacement Surgery<bold> is performed to restore healthy blood flow when blocked coronary arteries and damaged heart valves affect heart function. In one procedure, the surgeon uses a healthy blood vessel (graft) from another part of the body to bypass blocked arteries and also repairs or replaces diseased heart valves—improving overall heart performance.
singleBypassValveReplacement.description2: This combined surgery is often recommended when both coronary artery disease and valve issues are present. Techniques may include<bold> open-heart surgery</bold> or <bold>minimally invasive approaches</bold>, depending on the patient’s condition.
singleBypassValveReplacement.description3: Modern surgical advancements have greatly increased the safety and success rates of these procedures. Surgery typically lasts<bold> 2 to 4+ hours</bold>, depending on the number of valves treated.

mitralValveRepairReplacement.title: Mitral Valve Repair & Replacement Surgery
mitralValveRepairReplacement.subtitle: Learn how Mitral Valve Repair & Replacement Surgery can restore heart health. Trusted procedures, expert care at InDocsCare Medical Services
mitralValveRepairReplacement.description: <bold>Mitral valve repair and replacement surgery </bold>helps restore normal blood flow through the heart when the mitral valve is damaged or diseased. Located between the left heart chambers, this valve can leak (regurgitation) or narrow (stenosis), causing fatigue, breathlessness, and heart strain.
mitralValveRepairReplacement.surgicalPreference: Surgeons prefer<bold> valve repair </bold>to preserve heart function, but if the damage is severe, a full <bold>valve replacement </bold>with a mechanical or biological valve may be necessary.Depending on your condition, surgery can be performed via<bold> open-heart, minimally invasive, robotic-assisted,</bold> or<bold> catheter-based techniques.</bold>
mitralValveRepairReplacement.goalAndRecovery: The goal of this procedure is to relieve symptoms, improve heart performance, and enhance quality of life. Modern approaches mean faster recovery, with most patients returning to daily life in weeks, supported by cardiac rehab and lifestyle care.
